EXPLANATION:  
The spectrum shows the typical signature of a simple N,N-dialkyl amide.  
1. Very strong band at 739 cm⁻¹ – characteristic N(CH₃)₂ rocking/wagging vibration found near 730–740 cm⁻¹ in N,N-dimethyl-substituted amides such as N,N-dimethyl-acetamide (DMAc).  
2. Carbonyl stretch at 1639 cm⁻¹ – matches the amide-I (C=O) Raman band of tertiary acetamides, usually 1630–1660 cm⁻¹.  
3. Medium bands at 1416 cm⁻¹ and 1458 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ deformation modes (δ(CH₃)) of the two N-methyl groups, expected near 1 400–1 460 cm⁻¹.  
4. Doublet of strong C–H stretches at 2937 cm⁻¹ and 2821 cm⁻¹ – symmetric/antisymmetric stretching of the N-methyl and acetyl CH₃ groups, typical for small aliphatic amides.  
5. Supporting low-frequency bands at 594 cm⁻¹ (C–C–N deformation) and 961/1015 cm⁻¹ (C–N and CH₃ rocking) are all observed in reported Raman spectra of DMAc.

Among the candidates, molecule 1 (CC(=O)N(C)C) is exactly N,N-dimethylacetamide and provides the simplest structure that accounts for all these characteristic amide and N-methyl vibrations, whereas candidates containing Cl, S, or additional heteroatoms would be expected to introduce further distinctive bands (e.g., strong C–Cl or C–S stretches) not observed here.
